channel.title: The Luverne Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Luverne Journal (luvernejournal.com)

item.title: Memories from the Opelika Hospital
item.description: An Alabama pastor recalls learning of Reagan’s 1981 shooting at an Opelika hospital and an unexpected $20 bill that shaped his reflections on suffering, gratitude and God’s gifts.

item.title: Time with God sparks change
item.description: Pastor Dunford Cole reflects on how regular time with God visibly transforms believers — from renewed minds to changed daily lives — and why true encounters with God always leave a lasting mark.

item.title: McMeans shatters corrections career glass ceiling
item.description: After nearly seven years at Crenshaw County Detention, Sondra McMeans becomes the facility’s first assistant jail administrator and first Black woman in the role.

item.title: The fine print of ambition
item.description: An advice column on the fine line between healthy ambition and being “always available,” urging workers to question whether nonstop hustle is worth the personal cost.

item.title: Specialty crop grant applications open
item.description: Alabama agriculture department is accepting applications for USDA specialty crop block grants, offering $5,000–$40,000 for eligible commodity groups, organizations and institutions.

item.title: Regional Medical Center ownership launches recovery initiative
item.description: Regional Medical Center owners launch Sound Sobriety, a Luverne-based recovery program linking hospitals, mental health and addiction services across rural south Alabama.

item.title: Freshman leads Brantley past Wadley in Class 1A Boys’ Semifinal
item.description: Freshman 6-9 center Devin Melton powers Brantley past Wadley 62-47, sending the Bulldogs back to the Class 1A boys’ title game against Hubbertville at the AHSAA state championships.

item.title: EMA recognizes Mahone for leadership, service
item.description: Crenshaw County EMA honors Deputy Director Randy Mahone, its first African American employee, for six years of leadership and service during Black History Month.

item.title: This week in history: 1981
item.description: In 1981, Luverne pursued a $2 million federal grant to rebuild a blighted neighborhood while Glenwood Assembly of God held weeklong revival services with a traveling gospel family.

item.title: Middleton bids for Alabama Senate District 25 seat
item.description: Teacher and pastor KK Middleton launches bid for Alabama Senate District 25, promising improvements in health care, education, jobs and infrastructure for Montgomery and Crenshaw counties.
